The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Crypto Clarity Act barrels toward disappointment barring last-minute Senate turnaround. As the parties dig in their heels, the market structure bill hasn't yet amassed the votes it would need to clear the first Senate hurdle scheduled for Tuesday. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

European Central Bank calls for merchants to participate in digital euro pilot. The 12-month test will put a beta version of the central bank currency through online, mobile, in-store and peer-to-peer payments. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Clarity Act's odds of passing plunge as Republicans reject Democrats' counter-proposal. Prediction markets sharply marked down the crypto market structure bill’s near-term prospects as negotiations remained stuck hours before a key Senate vote. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

A hacker turned 25 cents of bitcoin into 46 billion fake BTC tokens on a DeFi bridge. Two software bugs allowed the attacker to create more than 2,000 times Bitcoin’s maximum supply in unbacked syBTC. Symbiosis puts preliminary losses at 9.97 BTC. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Standard Chartered predicts Arbitrum's ARB to rise 70-fold to $10, citing Robinhood Chain revenue. The bank expects tokenization to make Arbitrum a favored network for traditional finance, even though ARB holders currently have no direct claim on the fees. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

To ensure permanent economic innovation, we must pass the Clarity Act now. Congress needs 60 Senators willing to put innovation first and provide critical relief to the digital asset industry, argues Rep. Shri Thanedar (D-Mich.) Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $76,883 with a -2.46% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,432.24 with a -3.71% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

The Stablecoin Statement specifically addresses stablecoins that are designed to maintain a stable value relative to the US dollar (USD) on a one-for-one basis, [...] On December 16, 2025, the FDIC issued a notice of proposed rulemaking (the Proposal) to implement Section 5 of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act (GENIUS Act). The GENIUS Act, enacted by Congress in July 2025, created a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins whereby a subsidiary of an insured depository institution could be approved to issue payment stablecoins.

items.title: Cryptocurrency Regulation: A Guide to U.S. & Global Policies - Britannica
items.description:
Cryptocurrency regulation in the United States has historically been fragmented, with federal agencies applying different interpretations based on the nature and use of each asset. That splintered approach began to change in 2025, when Congress passed legislation to establish a clearer framework for stablecoins and digital asset markets.

## Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs [...] Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress made progress in 2025 toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. One measure—the GENIUS Act—was signed into law. [...] In the U.S., landmark legislation enacted in July 2025 has begun defining the roles of federal agencies in regulating stablecoins and digital commodities. Although implementation is ongoing, these laws represent a shift away from case-by-case enforcement and toward a structured national policy.
